_comment: State for the nightly DXEdge health check. Written by the scheduled Claude run at 9:00 PM PT. Read this first, write it back at the end of every run, including quiet nights.

cert.evidence: https://dxedge.net/api/health fetched cleanly over TLS at 04:19Z, no CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED and no expiry error
cert.notes: cert_repair.sh guard and /etc/cron.d/dxedge-certbot still in place. Exact expiry date not readable from this container: openssl sees the egress proxy certificate, not the real one.

main_dashboard.diagnosis: Unchanged and still NOT an outage. Both fields are passive cache reads; nothing repopulates them on a timer. See known_issues id health-metric-cold-cache. Do not re-investigate.

cyber_page.browser_check: not possible - no browser reachable. This scheduled run has no device bridge and no claude-in-chrome tools, so neither browser exists in the session. Fell back to exercising every feed through /api/feed as the runbook directs.
cyber_page.allowlist_gaps: none - every feed host on the page is already in ALLOWED_HOSTS. No allowlist change made or needed.

feeds_via_api_feed.cisa_advisories_all_xml: ok, 6 entries, first 'Rockwell Automation RSLinx Classic'
feeds_via_api_feed.cisa_kev_json: ok, catalogVersion 2026.09.01, count 1687. WebFetch reports the body truncated, but that is WebFetch's own content cap on a 1.7MB document, not the proxy: feedproxy reads to EOF before caching and MAX_BYTES is 4MB, and the cache key is present in /api/debug which only happens after a complete 200. Not a defect.
feeds_via_api_feed.nvd_2.0: could not be re-verified from this environment - the date-bearing URL is double-encoded and /api/feed answered 422, meaning the url param never arrived intact. Same environment limitation recorded 2026-09-01. Server-side evidence is good: the exact NVD query string appears as a live cache key in /api/debug, which is only written on a 200.
feeds_via_api_feed.krebs: ok, first entry 'Two Alleged TeamPCP Hackers Arrested in Australia'
feeds_via_api_feed.isc_sans: ok, ~10 entries, first 'ISC Stormcast For Tuesday, September 1st, 2026'

aethersdr_page.browser_check: not possible - same reason as cyber_page

runs.outbound_links_note: 27 curated links checked this run plus all 16 live feed endpoints. Link checking WORKED tonight, unlike 2026-09-01: WebFetch to third party hosts went through without an approval prompt. Whatever blocked it last night was transient, so do not assume Step 4 is permanently unavailable. 126 of 153 curated URLs remain unchecked; rotate through them on coming nights.
runs.outbound_links_uncheckable_reason: WebFetch force-upgrades http to https. These hosts are http-only, so the check fails for a reason that says nothing about whether the link works in a browser. kiwisdr.com additionally 302s https back to http, which is an unresolvable loop for this fetcher. Do not remove any of these on the strength of a failed fetch from this container.
problems_reported: 4 curated product links broken and repaired this run (see fixes_pushed)

known_issues_do_not_re_report.detail: sat_tles and pota_spots read 0 in /api/health whenever their caches are cold, which is most of the time. Cosmetic, not an outage. Only escalate if /api/pota or /api/satellites/positions themselves fail.

backend/tests/test_dxedge.py imports estimate_fof2 from voacap_engine, which does not define it. Confirmed still present 2026-09-02. Pre-existing break, not caused by the nightly run. Do not paper over by deleting the import.

nginx.conf limits /api/ to 30r/m burst 10 per IP and the cyber page fires several /api/feed calls per load. Nightly checks must pace their requests; this run used 4-request batches with 20-25s gaps and saw no throttling. Needs its own limit_req zone, which is a nginx.conf change and therefore an escalation, not an autonomous fix.

The cyber page's NVD query carries percent-encoded colons inside the url param. WebFetch re-encodes it and /api/feed answers 422 before the request reaches the upstream. This is a limitation of the checking environment, not a site defect. Verify NVD instead by looking for its cache key in /api/debug.

WebFetch reports the KEV JSON body as cut off mid-entry. That is WebFetch's own size cap on a 1.7MB document. feedproxy reads to EOF before caching and caps at 4MB. Do not re-open the truncation bug fixed in 3eb2ad8.

www.cisa.gov returns 403 to a direct WebFetch from this container but serves the same URLs fine through /api/feed, which sends a browser User-Agent. Check CISA feeds through the proxy, never directly.

The Mem note 'DXEdge - GitHub & Credentials' says the PAT expires ~August 27 2026. It authenticated and pushed successfully on 2026-09-02, so the note is wrong or the token was reissued. Harmless, but the note should be corrected so a future run does not skip repair work believing the token is dead.

awaiting_james.detail: Products.jsx vendor list entry 'KiwiSDR Network' points at https://sdr.hu, which returns 200 but only serves a shutdown notice: the project ended 2023-05-31. Not a 404 and not a dead host, so outside the autonomous repair mandate. Suggested replacement is http://kiwisdr.com/public/, the public KiwiSDR station list, but it could not be verified from this container because kiwisdr.com is http-only and 302s https back to http. Needs James to confirm the replacement URL, or say to drop the entry.

Three price fields no longer match the vendor page now linked. KiwiSDR 2 shows $299, vendor lists NZD 675 (roughly USD 400). Mobilinkd TNC4 shows $90, vendor lists $149.95. Xiegu G90 shows $400-450, xiegu.eu lists EUR 499 (roughly USD 588). Left untouched: prices may be deliberate street-price estimates rather than MSRP, and rewriting them is an editorial call, not link repair.

The M5Stack Cardputer link still resolves 200 but the vendor marks it End of Life and points to 'Cardputer-Adv'. Swapping it is a different product with different specs and price, which is a semantics change, so left alone pending James.
